items.t: REST PERIODS, WELLNESS BREAKS, AND MEAL BREAKS
l: Except for sections 340.01(E) and (F), this General Order is applicable to all full-duty sworn officers including appointed ranks.
1. If authorized by their immediate supervisor, sworn officers may take up to two (2) fifteen

(15) minute paid rest periods per normal working day, one during the first half and one during the second half of the workday. The fifteen (15) minute time for the rest period begins at the time a person leaves their workstation until they return to the workstation or if assigned to a vehicle, from the time they leave the vehicle until they return to the vehicle. Rest periods cannot be taken if personnel choose to take a forty-five (45) minute Wellness or Fitness break as defined below.
2. Sworn officers working special overtime assignments of less than four (4) hours shall not normally be allowed a rest period.
3. Sworn officers working four (4) hours or more but less than eight (8) hours may be allowed one (1) fifteen (15) minute rest period.
4. Rest periods shall not be taken in conjunction with meal breaks to extend the break time, nor shall rest periods be taken during the first or last hour of any shift.
5. For patrol officers, rest periods shall be taken in the officer’s assigned beat/area unless authorized by a sergeant or above.

6. During a rest period, sworn personnel witnessing a police emergency or called upon by a citizen to respond to an emergency shall immediately take action and not direct the citizen to call 911 for assistance.
1. Meal breaks shall be consistent with the length of time and compensation allowed by City policy or any authorized contract or agreement in effect.
2. Sworn officers working a normal workday, either eight (8) or ten (10) hours, may take one (1) paid forty-five (45) minute meal break.
3. Sworn officers working special overtime assignments of less than a normal workday (8 hours or 10 hours), but at least six (6) hours, may take one (1) thirty (30) minute meal break.

4. Meal breaks shall not be taken during the first or last hour of any shift unless approved by a sergeant or above. If approved to take a meal break in the first or last hour of any shift, the meal break shall not be used to shorten the shift or workday.

5. Non-uniformed and plain clothes officers on a paid meal break must wear a department-approved firearm and the police badge prominently displayed so as to be immediately recognizable as a Fort Worth Police Officer to be called upon by citizens in the event of an emergency.

6. Sworn personnel on a paid meal break who witness a police emergency or are called upon by a citizen to respond to an emergency shall immediately take action and not direct the citizen to call 911 for assistance.
7. Additional Criteria for Patrol Officers Meal Breaks:
a. Meal breaks will be requested through the dispatcher and only be taken when cleared by the dispatcher.

b. Officers must complete pending radio calls and return to service before proceeding to a meal break. This provision specifically prohibits going to a meal break location and finishing paperwork while on any call other than an authorized break.

c. Officers assigned to specific geographic beats/areas, temporarily or permanently, shall upon arrival at the break location, request clearance to take a break from the dispatcher and furnish a telephone number and/or location where they can be contacted. Other activities such as the ordering of meal, etc., before calling out, are prohibited.
d. Upon completion of a meal break, officers shall call in service to the dispatcher verbally and immediately exit the premises, and press the 10-24 button on the MDC when returning to the vehicle.
e. Meal breaks should be taken in the patrol officer's assigned area. Meal breaks in an adjacent area or division are permitted with prior permission from the officer’s supervisor.

1. Wellness or fitness breaks consist of one (1) forty-five (45) minute break to allow personnel time for exercising at an approved city exercise facility, to participate in one of the City of Fort Worth Employee Healthy Habits Fitness Classes listed in the City of Fort Worth Healthy Challenge Wellness Program, or other department-approved physical or mental Wellness Program.

2. Wellness or fitness breaks cannot be combined with any other break such as rest or meal breaks; however, the wellness or fitness break will not interfere with the time allotted for a meal break. There must be at least a two (2) hour separation between these breaks and both activities must be taken within the officer’s assigned geographical division, unless authorized by a supervisor.
3. If called into action, sworn officers must be able to actively respond within three (3) minutes to any emergency.

4. A wellness or fitness break must be approved by the employee's supervisor and must not interfere with normal duty performance. This break can be canceled and future approval denied if an employee is found to be in a violation of this policy.
D. Number of marked units and officers permitted at one location, excluding police facilities:
1. The maximum number of marked police units allowed at one location for the purpose of taking a meal break or rest period is two (2), regardless of what unit the officers are assigned.
2. The maximum number of uniformed officers allowed at one location for the purpose of taking a meal break or rest period shall be no more than four (4) officers, excluding supervisors.

3. In circumstances, including, but not limited to, team meetings, special occasions, training, etc., the officers' sergeant or above may temporarily waive this section. Permanent waivers issued from the applicable Bureau Assistant Chief must be in writing.

If a bureau or division's rest period or meal break procedures become unworkable, the deputy chief or civilian equivalent over the area in need of modification shall prepare and submit a workable procedure for approval through the applicable interoffice form to the Chief of Police.

F. Since sworn officers placed in restricted or transitional duty statuses are reassigned to alternative duties and are precluded from wearing the police uniform or uniform equipment thus making them unable to be called upon in an emergency situation, they will be given an alternative nine (9) or eleven (11) hour work schedule with a one (1) hour uncompensated meal break.

G. Unless specifically approved by the Chief of Police through written interoffice correspondence for unit approval, all General Employees shall take rest periods and meal breaks in accordance with the City of Fort Worth Personnel Rules and Regulations for General Employees.

Officers shall advise the dispatcher that they require a court call and specify the court they shall be attending. Officers shall appear promptly and after being released, should leave the building, clearing the call. Officers shall follow standard procedure regarding court attendance as outlined in GO 406.04 Court Appearances and Hearings.

The officer shall call the dispatcher and advise that they shall require a tire truck. The officer shall be required to provide the location, car make, and equipment number, and shall clear their call immediately after a flat tire is changed.

A. The total time an officer shall be permitted on a garage call at any equipment services facility shall be forty-five (45) minutes. When the repairs and/or maintenance require in excess of forty-five (45) minutes, the officer shall contact a supervisor. The supervisor may approve additional time or advise the officer to obtain another unit. Once the garage completes the necessary repairs/maintenance, the officer shall verbally clear the call and advise the dispatcher that they shall be en route to their beat or assignment (i.e., Staff 3, I’m back in service 10-24).
B. If a unit is disabled, the officer shall contact their respective dispatcher.

1. The officer shall be required to provide the equipment number, make of the vehicle, and current location. The dispatch coordinator, when notifying the Equipment Services Division, shall ascertain the estimated time of arrival (ETA) of the garage unit.

2. If the officer is advised by the dispatcher that the ETA exceeds one (1) hour, then it is the responsibility of the officer to contact a supervisor to ascertain whether to stand by or take immediate steps to obtain another vehicle.

Officers shall request this type of call when in need of radio repair. Once Radio Services completes the necessary repairs/maintenance, the officer shall verbally clear the call and advise the dispatcher that they are en route to their beat or assignment (i.e., Staff 3, I’m back in service 10-24).
Unless otherwise directed, officers dispatched to this type of call shall report to the appropriate division office.

To terminate duty before the end of a normal shift requires a supervisor’s approval. The officer securing the unit shall advise the dispatcher as soon as possible after receiving the permission, and state under whose authority this request was granted. In some cases, when air traffic is heavy, this notification may be completed by telephone.

items.t: CALL FOR CRIME SCENE SEARCH UNIT
l: This type of call is used when officers need to request a crime scene search unit at the scene of an offense.
